To preserve chemical integrity and prevent degradation, we recommend storing lyophilized compounds at -20°C for long-term study, or 2–8°C for immediate short-term use. Avoid repetitive freeze-thaw cycles and reconstitute only using sterile Bacteriostatic Water.

HPLC reports showing exact purity graphs and Mass Spectrometry structural confirmations are fully accessible by B2B buyers upon request prior to fulfillment.

faqs.q: Is a medical prescription required to purchase research peptides?

However, you must certify that all procured compounds will be used strictly for laboratory research, academic in-vitro study, and scientific investigation. These compounds are strictly not for human or animal consumption.

FAQ.title: Quality & Testing FAQ
FAQ.subtitle: Detailed answers to the most common questions about our purity standards, analytical methodology, Freedom Diagnostic verification, and COA documentation process.

items.q: What does ≥99% purity mean for wholesale research peptides?
items.a: Purity ≥99% means at least 99 of every 100 molecules in a given vial are the correctly sequenced target peptide. This threshold — verified by reversed-phase HPLC and LC-MS analysis at [Freedom Diagnostic](https://freedomdiagnostic.com) — rules out truncated sequences, synthesis impurities, and oxidation byproducts that can distort assay results. Industry convention considers anything below 98% unsuitable for reliable in-vitro or in-vivo research use.

items.q: Who is Freedom Diagnostic and what role do they play?
items.a: Freedom Diagnostic is our named independent U.S. analytical laboratory. Every production batch is physically shipped to their facility, where HPLC and LC-MS instrumentation confirms both peptide sequence identity and purity percentage before any product ships from our warehouse. Results are issued as a batch-matched Certificate of Analysis — tied to a specific lot number, not a generic reference standard.

items.q: What is a batch-matched Certificate of Analysis (COA)?
items.a: A batch-matched COA is a laboratory test report generated for a specific production lot — not a template, generic document, or reused result. It lists the compound name, lot number, HPLC chromatogram, mass spectrometry data, and confirmed purity percentage. Every order from 99 Purity Wholesale ships with the COA corresponding to that exact batch, so you can trace the document back to the same vials you received.

items.q: What is the difference between HPLC and LC-MS in peptide testing?
items.a: Reversed-phase HPLC (High-Performance Liquid Chromatography) separates compounds by hydrophobicity and measures purity as a percentage of the total integrated peak area. LC-MS (Liquid Chromatography–Mass Spectrometry) adds molecular weight confirmation, verifying that the detected compound has the correct sequence identity — not just that a pure compound is present. Using both methods together is the analytical gold standard for research-grade peptides.

items.q: Do all compounds in your catalog come with a COA?
items.a: Yes. Every compound listed in our [product catalog](/products) is assigned a batch-matched COA from Freedom Diagnostic before it is made available for wholesale purchase. We do not offer products that have not passed independent purity verification. The COA document ships with your order and is also available for pre-order review on request.

items.q: How is peptide purity different from peptide potency?
items.a: Purity describes what percentage of the material is the intended peptide compound versus impurities. Potency describes how biologically active that compound is in a specific assay context. A peptide can be ≥99% pure but still exhibit variable potency depending on reconstitution protocol, storage conditions, and the research application. 99 Purity Wholesale guarantees purity as verified by analytical instrumentation — potency for a specific research endpoint is outside the scope of COA documentation.

items.q: Are your peptides manufactured in a GMP-compliant facility?
items.a: Our compounds are synthesized in a U.S.-based facility using solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS). Independent third-party verification through Freedom Diagnostic serves as our primary quality assurance mechanism. We do not hold an FDA drug manufacturing license, as our products are supplied strictly for licensed research use — not for human administration. We apply rigorous synthesis and handling standards consistent with research-grade supply.

items.q: What happens if a batch fails to meet ≥99% purity?
items.a: Any production lot that fails the ≥99% purity threshold in Freedom Diagnostic testing is rejected and not released into the wholesale catalog. We do not discount or remarket failing batches under any circumstances. Only lots with a passing COA are made available for order. This no-exceptions rejection policy is the foundation of our quality guarantee to [wholesale accounts](/services#pricing).

items.q: How long are COA documents valid and how should they be stored?
items.a: A COA reflects the purity of a batch at the time of testing and does not expire as a document — it is a permanent record tied to that lot number. However, actual compound integrity is affected by storage conditions over time. We recommend storing lyophilized peptides sealed at -20°C for long-term stability, retaining the COA as a reference document throughout your research project.

items.q: Can I request a sample COA before placing a wholesale order?
items.a: Yes. Prospective wholesale accounts can request sample COA documentation for any compound in our catalog prior to submitting an order. Contact our B2B team via [WhatsApp](https://wa.me/18433307365) or email at [sales@99puritywholesale.com](mailto:sales@99puritywholesale.com) to request the batch documentation for your compound of interest.

items.a: Most overseas suppliers operate at 95%–98% purity standards, with COAs produced by in-house or affiliated labs — a fundamental conflict of interest. 99 Purity Wholesale uses exclusively independent third-party testing through Freedom Diagnostic, enforces a ≥99% minimum with no exceptions, and ships from within the U.S. with no customs exposure. See our [full comparison table](/quality#comparison) for a structured breakdown.

items.q: What is solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS)?
items.a: SPPS is the industry-standard method for manufacturing research peptides. Amino acids are assembled sequentially on a solid resin support, building the target peptide chain one residue at a time. This method allows precise control over sequence fidelity and minimizes the byproduct profile. hplc.definition: The primary analytical chemistry technique used to separate, identify, and quantify each component in a mixture. At 99 Purity Wholesale, we use HPLC to verify that our research compounds exceed the ≥99% purity threshold.

lyophilized.title: Lyophilized
lyophilized.definition: The process of freeze-drying a compound to remove water while preserving its chemical structure. This results in a stable, powdered form that is ideal for long-term storage and transport without requiring a constant cold chain.

glp1-agonist.title: GLP-1 Agonist
glp1-agonist.definition: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 receptor agonists are a class of research compounds that mimic the GLP-1 hormone. In research settings, these are studied for their effects on glucose metabolism, insulin secretion, and appetite regulation.

secretagogue.title: Secretagogue
secretagogue.definition: A substance that promotes secretion. In peptide research, growth hormone secretagogues (GHS) like Ipamorelin or CJC-1295 are studied for their ability to stimulate the pituitary gland to release endogenous growth hormone.

moq.title: MOQ (Minimum Order Quantity)
moq.definition: The smallest amount of a product that a wholesale supplier is willing to sell. For 99 Purity Wholesale, our MOQ is typically 10 units (1 kit), which allows us to maintain competitive wholesale pricing for professional clients.

coa.title: COA (Certificate of Analysis)
coa.definition: A document issued by an analytical laboratory that confirms a product meets its quality specifications. Our COAs include HPLC and Mass Spectrometry data to prove purity and identity.

dac.title: DAC (Drug Affinity Complex)
dac.definition: A technology used to increase the half-life of a peptide by allowing it to bind to albumin in the bloodstream. CJC-1295 with DAC has a significantly longer duration of action in research models compared to CJC-1295 without DAC.

no-dac.title: No-DAC (CJC-1295 without DAC / Mod GRF 1-29)
no-dac.definition: The version of CJC-1295 that does not include the Drug Affinity Complex. It has a shorter half-life and is often preferred in research where precise control over growth hormone pulses is required.

spps.title: SPPS (Solid-Phase Peptide Synthesis)
spps.definition: The standard method for chemical peptide synthesis. It involves building a peptide chain by adding amino acids one by one while the chain is tethered to a solid support. This method is used in our U.S. facility for high-purity production.

research-grade.title: Research Grade
research-grade.definition: A specification indicating that a compound is intended exclusively for laboratory research and is not for human or animal consumption. Our research-grade peptides are produced to the highest analytical standards (≥99%).

hgh.title: HGH (Human Growth Hormone)
hgh.definition: A hormone produced by the pituitary gland that stimulates growth, cell reproduction, and cell regeneration. Many peptides in our catalog are studied for their role as HGH secretagogues.

peptide-api.title: Peptide API (Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient)
peptide-api.definition: The pure peptide compound used as the active component in research formulations. We supply bulk APIs to compounding pharmacies and researchers.

purity-threshold.title: Purity Threshold

cas-number.title: CAS Number

faqs.q: What is the primary grade of these compounds?
faqs.a: All compounds are analytical reference standards synthesized at a purity level of ≥99.0%, verified by HPLC and Mass Spectrometry.

faqs.q: Are these peptides intended for human consumption?
faqs.a: No. Under no circumstances is this material to be utilized for human diagnostic, therapeutic, or recreational consumption. Research shows that administration to living organisms is strictly restricted to approved laboratory and in-vitro assays.

faqs.q: How does research show these peptides should be stored?
faqs.a: Research shows that lyophilized peptides are stable at room temperature for short periods, but must be stored at -20°C for long-term stability. Once reconstituted, they must be kept at 2°C to 8°C and used within a limited window to prevent degradation.

faqs.q: What is reconstitution and what solvent should be used?
faqs.a: Reconstitution is the process of dissolving the lyophilized powder. Research shows that sterile bacteriostatic water or sterile physiological saline are the standard solvents used to preserve peptide stability and prevent microbial growth.

faqs.q: What does the HPLC chromatogram represent?
faqs.a: The HPLC (High-Performance Liquid Chromatography) chromatogram represents the molecular purity profile of the batch. Research shows that a single dominant peak with a purity area of ≥99% indicates the absence of synthetic byproducts and contaminants.

faqs.q: Can these research compounds be combined in a single study?
faqs.a: Yes. Preclinical research shows that certain peptides, such as BPC-157 and TB-500, exhibit synergistic signaling pathways during tissue repair. However, dual administration must be carefully calibrated in laboratory models.

faqs.q: Why is molar mass and molecular formula variance important?
faqs.a: Molecular formula and molar mass are fingerprinted identifiers. Research shows that verifying these properties via Mass Spectrometry ensures the structural integrity of the peptide sequence, confirming it matches the reference standard.

faqs.q: What documentation is provided for regulatory compliance?
